items.label: text
items.text: During the manufacture of nitric acid from ammonia, the ammonia is oxidised to nitrogen monoxide, NO, by oxygen in the air.

items.label: formula
items.text: 4 N H _ { 3 } ( g ) + 5 O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 4 N O ( g ) + 6 H _ { 2 } O ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: The ammonia is mixed with air and passed through a stack of large circular gauzes made of platinum-rhodium alloy at red heat (about 900 °C). The platinum-rhodium gauzes act as a catalyst for the reaction.

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Gas particles have to collide before they can react. Use the collision theory to help you to answer the following questions.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Because the gases are in contact with the catalyst for only a very short time, it is important that the reaction happens as quickly as possible. Explain why increasing the temperature to 900 °C makes the reaction very fast. (ε)

items.label: list_item
items.text: ii Explain what will happen to the reaction rate if the pressure is increased. (2)
